items.item_text: Previous experience performing adult echocardiography in a hospital-based inpatient setting.
Experience with critically ill patients and complex cardiovascular conditions.
Experience assisting with TEE and stress echocardiography examinations.
Experience working independently during weekends, holidays, or shifts with reduced staffing.

UCLA Health is seeking an experienced Per Diem Echocardiographic Technician to join our Non-Invasive Cardiodiagnostics team. Responsibilities include independently performing comprehensive adult echocardiograms, recognizing and communicating abnormal findings, administering ultrasound enhancing agents as indicated and within scope of practice, assisting with TEE and stress echocardiograms, and ensuring accurate documentation, patient safety, and quality care.
A minimum of three years of clinical adult echocardiography experience is required.

This position primarily supports weekend coverage and requires availability on weekends, holidays, and occasional weekdays. This position supports cardiology services within our Santa Monica and Westwood locations. Rotations within this region are sometimes necessary and required to accommodate staffing needs.
Successful completion of a cardiac echocardiography technology program.
Registered (ARDMS ) in adult cardiac echocardiography (AE) RDCS or pediatric echocardiography (PE) RDCS.
Knowledge and ability to apply knowledge of cardiac anatomy, physiology, and pathophysiology.
Familiarity with echocardiography reporting and digital image management systems.
Ability to apply theory to practice in the application of ultrasound technique to the clinical evaluation of the target anatomy.
Ability to push the 500+ lb. echo machine for distances up to 100 feet within the office.
Skill and manual dexterity to manipulate transducer and buttons, and knobs on the echo machine to obtain optimal studies.
Knowledge, skill, and ability to use P.C. and word processing software to generate written preliminary reports.
Knowledge, skill, and ability to make preliminary evaluations of echo studies to generate written preliminary reports.
Ability to prepare and maintain log of procedures, track charge documents, compare activity records, and determine that all studies are billed and collected for.
Ability to work independently and complete tasks in a timely manner with minimal to no direction.
Strong interpersonal skills to effectively interact with patients, physicians, nurses, staff, and others in a professional and courteous manner.
Ability to read, interpret, apply, and/or follow physician orders, policies, procedures, or written and verbal instructions.
Ability to deliver basic cardiac life support (BCLS).
